quality_guards: Electrical controls depend on voltage, energy, equipment, environment, task complexity, isolation options and worker competence.
Electrical-safety evidence is installation-, equipment- and task-specific and is not an exact parcel-level incident probability.
Asbestos controls depend on building responsibility, materials, accessibility, condition and planned work.
Asbestos evidence is building-, material- and activity-specific and is not an exact parcel-level exposure probability.
Legionella controls depend on the water system, temperatures, aerosol generation, stagnation, users, susceptibility and operating regime.
Legionella evidence is water-system-, operation- and population-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Work-at-height controls depend on task, height, duration, access, surface strength, weather, rescue arrangements and competence.
Work-at-height evidence is task-, equipment- and condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fall probability.
Drone requirements depend on weight, class, camera, category, people, location and current airspace restrictions.
Drone-safety evidence is aircraft-, operation-, location- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level aviation-risk probability.
Level-crossing risk depends on crossing type, users, traffic, trains, visibility, behaviour, land use and control performance.
Level-crossing evidence is crossing-, user- and operating-condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collision probability.
Environmental reporting depends on incident type, jurisdiction, regulated status, immediate danger and emergency-service need.
Environmental-incident guidance is event-, location- and jurisdiction-specific and is not an exact parcel-level pollution probability.
Medical-device action depends on the exact device, model, batch, software version, notice, users and current manufacturer instructions.
Medical-device evidence is device-, incident- and user-specific and is not an exact parcel-level patient-safety probability.
Protective-security measures depend on threat, venue, event, crowd flows, assets, vulnerabilities, intelligence and capability.
Protective-security evidence is threat-, venue- and event-specific and is not an exact parcel-level attack probability.
Priority services depend on current needs, supplier, network operator and gas or electricity arrangements.
Priority-services evidence is household-, need- and provider-specific and is not an exact parcel-level outage-impact probability.
